outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}x+112^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=180^{\circ}-112^{\circ}\\x&=68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}y+32.5^{\circ}+46.75^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\y+79.25^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\y&=100.75^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Subtract the known angle from $180^{\circ}$ because the two angles fill a straight angle.
$\begin{aligned}a+146^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\a&=180^{\circ}-146^{\circ}\\a&=34^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

$137^{\circ}+45^{\circ}=182^{\circ}$.
Angles on one side of a straight line must total $180^{\circ}$, so $PQR$ cannot be straight.

examples.derivation: The adjacent sectors total 180°. Thus x = 180° − 112° = 68°. The ray at 112° leaves a 68° sector.
The supplement is 180° − 76.5° = 103.5°. The opening expression and following equals sign have matching alignment markers and the required phantom gutter. No diagram is needed.
a + 146° = 180°, hence a = 34°. Adding 146° to 180° does not find the remaining sector. The diagram's sectors measure 146° and 34°.
137° + 45° = 182°, which exceeds a straight angle by 2°. QP has direction 182° and QS has direction 45°, giving the marked 137° sector; QR has direction 0°. PQR is therefore not straight.
